answer.rationale: Memory 57 is strongest because it directly reports qualified-revenue gains with no measurable retention harm, although long-term cohort economics and incentive costs are not stated. Memory 44 has strong relevance to qualified pipeline, but omits closed-won revenue, sales cost, retention, and lifetime value. Memories 31 and 86 support leading indicators of sustainable revenue through activation and time-to-value, but do not establish downstream qualification, monetization, or retention. Memory 91 is further removed, reporting week-one engagement and first meaningful action without revenue or retention outcomes. Memory 73 is least supported for the sustainable long-term objective: it reports acquisition and revenue lift from promotional pricing, but omits discount durability, margin, retention, expansion, and whether acquired accounts remain qualified; aggressive pricing can also undermine long-term economics.
